hints: Focus on the real bonding in nitrogen and the real chemistry of ammonia in water, not just memorised phrases.
Remember each nitrogen atom in $\text{N}_2$ does have a lone pair, $\text{N}_2$ has a very strong triple bond, and ammonia reacts reversibly with water.
Ask yourself which species can donate a proton ($\text{H}^+$) and which oxides actually form photochemical smog with hydrocarbons in sunlight.
walkthrough:
**Recall why nitrogen is so unreactive**

Think structure first. Each N atom in $\text{N}_2$ has a lone pair, so lack of lone pairs is not the reason.

The real reason is the very strong triple bond:
$$\text{N} \equiv \text{N}$$

**Check aqueous ammonia equilibrium**

When ammonia dissolves it does not stay only as $\text{NH}_3$. It sets up a reversible base equilibrium with water.

$$\text{NH}_3(\text{aq}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq})$$
So both $\text{NH}_3(\text{aq})$ and $\text{NH}_4^+(\text{aq})$ are present.

**Decide if $\text{NH}_4^+$ is a Bronsted-Lowry acid**

A Bronsted-Lowry acid is a proton ($\text{H}^+$) donor. $\text{NH}_4^+$ can donate a proton to reform $\text{NH}_3$.

$$\text{NH}_4^+(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3(\text{aq}) + \text{H}^+(\text{aq})$$
This confirms the statement about aqueous ammonia is correct.

**Eliminate the other two statements**

Nitrogen has a triple bond, not a double bond, so any mention of double bonds is wrong. Photochemical smog comes from nitrogen oxides ($\text{NO}_x$) with unburnt hydrocarbons in sunlight, not from $\text{SO}_2$ which causes acid rain.

options.A: False. $\text{N}_2$ is unreactive because of the very high bond energy of the $\text{N} \equiv \text{N}$ triple bond, not because of missing lone pairs. In fact each N atom in $\text{N}_2$ has one lone pair (:N triple bond N:).
options.B: Correct. Aqueous ammonia is a weak base equilibrium containing both $\text{NH}_3(\text{aq})$ and $\text{NH}_4^+(\text{aq})$. The $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion can act as a Bronsted-Lowry acid by donating $\text{H}^+$ to form $\text{NH}_3$.
options.C: False. High temperature is needed to break the strong triple bond in $\text{N}_2$, for example in lightning or car engines forming $\text{NO}_x$. Calling it a double bond is incorrect.
options.D: False. Photochemical smog is formed when nitrogen oxides ($\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$) react with unburnt hydrocarbons in sunlight to form ozone and PAN. $\text{SO}_2$ leads mainly to acid rain, not photochemical smog.
